signature.name: The Bund
signature.detail: Shanghai's iconic waterfront promenade, lined with historic colonial-era buildings facing the Pudong skyline across the Huangpu River. It is the single must-see for any first-time visitor. Go early in the morning or after dark when the skyline is lit; it is free and open all day, reachable by metro to East Nanjing Road.

signature.name: Yu Garden
signature.detail: A classical Ming-dynasty garden with rockeries, pavilions and ponds in the old city. Pair it with the surrounding Yuyuan Bazaar for snacks and shopping. Arrive at opening to avoid crowds; small admission fee applies.

signature.name: Oriental Pearl Tower
signature.detail: The futuristic tower that defined Pudong's skyline, with observation decks and a glass floor. Best visited on a clear day for views over the river and the Bund. Book tickets ahead and go near sunset to see both day and night views.

signature.name: Shanghai Tower
signature.detail: China's tallest skyscraper, with a high-speed lift to an observation deck offering sweeping views of the city. Go on a clear day; tickets are sold on site and online, and late afternoon gives the best light.

signature.name: Nanjing Road
signature.detail: Shanghai's famous pedestrian shopping street running from People's Square toward the Bund. It is a lively place to stroll, shop and people-watch. Visit in the evening when the neon lights are on; it is free and easy to reach by metro.

signature.name: People's Square
signature.detail: The central civic square and transport hub, surrounded by the Shanghai Museum and Grand Theatre. A convenient starting point for exploring the city center. It is free and open; metro lines converge here.

signature.name: Shanghai Museum
signature.detail: A leading museum of Chinese art and antiquities, including bronzes, ceramics and calligraphy. Admission is free but advance booking is often required. Allow a couple of hours; it sits right on People's Square.

signature.name: Xintiandi
signature.detail: A restored shikumen lane district turned into a stylish pedestrian area of cafes, shops and restaurants. Good for an evening stroll and people-watching. It is free to wander and reachable by metro.

signature.name: Shanghai World Financial Center
signature.detail: A distinctive bottle-opener-shaped skyscraper with an observation deck and a glass-floor walkway high above Pudong. Visit on a clear day; tickets are available on site and online.

transport: Metro about $0.5-1 a ride; taxis affordable
